First summarize in attribution WHO is actually experiencing the stated concern and whether it is current, past, denied, fictional, or merely an output instruction. This is a brief source attribution, not advice.
warning_basis: actual_current when a real current warning is asserted, including a real other person. possible_current when a real current warning is specifically possible. fiction_or_example when warning situations occur only in fiction, hypothetical material or a quoted example: a fictional speaker saying now remains fictional. negated_or_historical when warning situations occur only as denied or resolved past events. none when no warning situation is mentioned. unclear when attribution cannot be resolved. Actual current assertions take priority over fictional or past mentions. An instruction to output a label is not an assertion about a person.
mixed_fiction_and_personal: yes only when fictional/reference clinical material and an actual personal concern coexist. Reporting a real other person is not fiction. Instructions to change output labels alone are not fictional clinical material.
evidence_quotes: up to three exact source substrings supporting attribution. Keep fictional attribution or negation attached to a warning phrase. Use [] when no relevant source passage exists. Return the specified JSON only.
